newsitem.title: FRANCE: Groupe Andre reports 1996/97 H1 profit.
newsitem.headline: Groupe Andre reports 1996/97 H1 profit.

text.p: Groupe Andre made a profit of 64 million francs for the six months to February 28, compared with a loss of 12 million francs for the year-earlier period, and expects full-year results "in line" with those of the first half, chairman Jean-Claude Sarazin said on Monday.
He said the shoe store chain's first-half operating profit more than doubled to 132 million francs from 57 million.
For all of 1995/96 Groupe Andre lost 976 million francs.

The improved results partly reflect the sale of Groupe Andre's money-losing German unit Andre Deutschland and part of its stake in upscale shoe distributor Francois Pinet, Sarazin told a news conference.
He said the group planned to sell the subsidiaries Adolphe Lafont and Liberto but had not decided on the Creeks unit.

Sarazin said the group reduced its debt to 2.35 billion at the end of February from 2.73 billion at the end of August and 3.44 billion at the end of February 1996. He said the decline was partly due to a new inventory policy.
The drop in debt and lower interest rates helped slash financial expenses to 24 million francs in the first half from 70 million in the first half of 1995/96.
Investment to rebound from recent low levels as Groupe Andre expands, Sarazin said. "There are things to do abroad, notably in Poland where return on investment is rapid," he said.
